exam.title: Red Hat Certified Advanced System Administrator in Ansible
exam.study_prerequisites: Red Hat recommends RHCSA-level RHEL administration plus AU294 or comparable Ansible experience. Confirm the exact purchasable exam version; the current AU294 public baseline is RHEL 10, Ansible Core 2.16 and development tooling aligned with AAP 2.5/2.6. Practice reproducible fresh-host playbooks, navigator/execution environments, Git/VS Code, roles/collections, Vault and persistent automation of RHCSA tasks.

objective_coverage.objective_group: RHCSA capability and simple shell-script analysis
Run and develop playbooks with navigator, Git and VS Code

review.notes: The current unweighted EX294 objectives were reconciled with the AU294 RHEL 10, Ansible Core 2.16, and AAP 2.5/2.6 training baseline. The guide preserves Red Hat's warning that multiple exam versions may be sold, separates the current Advanced System Administrator in Ansible name from older RHCE branding, and treats evaluation as reproducible playbooks applied to fresh systems. Three scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks cover inventory and controller configuration, execution environments and collections, navigator, Git/VS Code development containers, modules and resilient playbooks, roles, RHEL administration, templates, Vault, idempotence, second-run evidence and fresh-host replay. All eight URLs are cataloged: five reachable and three commercial routes automation-blocked; none missing or broken. Older material has an explicit current-page gap checklist and no recalled exam tasks are used.

findings.title: Upstream latest documentation is not the assigned EE runtime
findings.evidence: Lifecycle table lists core 2.16 as AAP 2.6 default with separate streams and product support.
findings.recommendation: Pin core references for this baseline and verify the actual EE; do not infer product support from upstream banners.
findings.resolution: Pin core references for this baseline and verify the actual EE; do not infer product support from upstream banners.

findings.title: Effective configuration selection was too abstract
findings.evidence: First applicable configuration file wins and world-writable cwd is not automatically trusted.
findings.recommendation: List selection order and concrete inspection commands in the actual execution context.
findings.resolution: List selection order and concrete inspection commands in the actual execution context.

findings.title: Failure reporting can hide wrong state
findings.evidence: Condition lists AND together; changed_when changes reporting rather than command side effects.
findings.recommendation: Add a four-case OR/AND matrix and accurate reporting boundaries.
findings.resolution: Add a four-case OR/AND matrix and accurate reporting boundaries.

findings.title: Recovery needs a verified target state
findings.evidence: Successful rescue permits continuation without automatic rollback; unreachable or malformed tasks differ from returned task failures.
findings.recommendation: Explain failure categories and explicit failure after diagnostic-only recovery.
findings.resolution: Explain failure categories and explicit failure after diagnostic-only recovery.

findings.title: Handler execution was overgeneralized in supplemental material
findings.evidence: Later failures can suppress notified handlers; handlers can run again after a flush if notified again.
findings.recommendation: Use current per-flush semantics and reject the historical blog once-per-playbook generalization.
findings.resolution: Use current per-flush semantics and reject the historical blog once-per-playbook generalization.

findings.title: Templates needed an executable validation example
findings.evidence: The module validates a temporary candidate; valid text can still encode incorrect intent from a string boolean.
findings.recommendation: Add original inventory/playbook/template/Python validator and test input type plus output format independently.
findings.resolution: Add original inventory/playbook/template/Python validator and test input type plus output format independently.

findings.title: Check mode and secret-output boundaries needed precision
findings.evidence: Task overrides may execute real changes during --check; diff can expose candidate content.
findings.recommendation: Inspect module support/overrides and separate previews from actual runs, using output controls for secrets.
findings.resolution: Inspect module support/overrides and separate previews from actual runs, using output controls for secrets.

findings.title: Knowledge checks lacked answers
findings.evidence: All 40 original questions previously had no worked answers.
findings.recommendation: Add answers and explicit local-versus-platform validation boundaries.
findings.resolution: Add answers and explicit local-versus-platform validation boundaries.

blog_intake.value: Repeatable desired state, explicit names and reusable role interfaces.
blog_intake.limits: Historical article, not current version guidance. Do not adopt once-per-playbook handler timing or treat role dependencies as safely unpinned; primary docs and explicit inputs govern.

local_validation.execution_boundary: Actual local Jinja/PyYAML parsing and rendering, raw-expression evaluation, and original Python candidate validator execution on owned temporary files. Ansible task execution, module template validation hook, inventory precedence, SSH, navigator/EE, RHEL services/storage/security, Vault encryption and fresh-host/reboot labs were not executed.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.
Local Jinja 3.1.6 and PyYAML 6.0.3 do not emulate all Ansible filters, templating, inventory/variable precedence or module execution.
No ansible-playbook, navigator, EE, SSH, Vault encryption or RHEL administration/reboot/fresh-host labs executed; all eight platform labs remain proposed. Prior WSL startup blocker remains deferred.
Two Udemy pages and OReilly book page blocked automated access; inherited runtime/date/item counts were not reverified.
Public current objectives and course baseline do not establish an individual assigned exam version, exact available EE image or appointment metadata.
